comment: Shared path-grammar cases, read by BOTH sides of the picker contract:
tests/test_path_grammar_parity.py drives the special agent's own resolver,
frontend/src/lib/jsonpaths.test.ts drives the wizard's TypeScript port.
A path the operator clicks in the picker has to mean in the check exactly
what the wizard previewed, so the two implementations answer the same
cases from one file instead of each side's tests asserting its own idea.
Only WELL-FORMED paths live here: for a malformed path the two differ on
purpose (the port refuses it, the agent's tokenizer skips the junk), which
each side's own tests pin down.

cases.name: a leading $ is the document root
a bare $ prefix without the dot
an index past the end matches nothing
a key holding null is found, with the null
a wildcard over an object map
a wildcard reaching deeper into each element
two wildcard levels expand to the cartesian product
a wildcard over an empty array matches nothing
a wildcard over a missing container matches nothing
a bracket-quoted key holding a dot
a double-quoted key holding a dot
a double-quoted key holding an apostrophe
